title: Iron Road: Steam Railway Sound Effects
shortText: 109 steam railway sound effects: locomotive at six speeds, whistles, carriage, station, signal box. WAV + OGG.
html:
One working steam railway, at six speeds

109 railway sounds built from one set of iron, steel, brass, oak, glass and bronze models: the locomotive exhaust and the rail joints at six speeds as seamless loops, whistles, steam and brakes, the footplate, the carriage, the station, the signal box and the level crossing, and 25 seamless loops in all.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No credit required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as sounds. The full plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 21 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. Three of the six speeds (the exhaust and the rails), the same whistle heard from the footplate, a compartment and the platform, and the locomotive's whole lifecycle.

What is in it

  • Locomotive (10)
  • Rails and wheels (14)
  • Whistles and bell (6)
  • Steam and brakes (8)
  • Footplate (14)
  • Carriage (10)
  • Couplings and shunting (6)
  • Station platform (8)
  • Signal box (9)
  • Level crossing (4)
  • Heard from three rooms (15)
  • Place beds (5)

Six speeds, counted

The exhaust beats four times for every turn of the wheels, and the rail joints pass under the carriage two axles and two bogies at a time. Both ship as seamless loops at six speeds, from about 11 km/h to about 106 km/h, and every loop's beats and clacks are counted out of the shipped file and must match the design or the build fails. Step a train through the rungs as it speeds up and the rhythm is right at each one. 10 ladder steps, every one climbing in brightness.

Heard from three places

A whistle, a brake, the safety valve, a coupling and a tunnel entry, each heard from the footplate, from inside a compartment and from the platform. Files are named event_from_place, so when the camera moves you change one word. Measured on the shipped files: 15 place pairs and 30 event pairs, 0 too close.

Three lifecycles

Locomotive, Injector, Level crossing: each ships its start, a seamless loop while it runs, its stop and the way it fails (the wheels slip, the injector knocks off, a gate jams). 12 states, every loop flag read out of the file.

Already own Pithead or Escapement?

Every one of the 11 roles Iron Road shares with Pithead was measured against it from both packs' files, and each is a different sound. Every one of the 11 roles Iron Road shares with Escapement was measured against it from both packs' files, and each is a different sound. So owning all three gives you three sets of sounds, not one twice.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a manifest listing every file by slot.
  • 25 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in the WAV and the OGG. Checked in a blank Godot 4 project: the WAV

loops import looping with default settings.

  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 3.35 dB.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 1017 checks, 0 failed.
  • Nothing in it is music: a whistle is one object sounding, a bell is struck, so it sits under any soundtrack.

Honest limits

These are synthesised railway sounds, not field recordings of a real locomotive. The measurements above are signal measurements, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Pithead: The Working Mine, one mine in three rooms, the line's last entry.
  • Leeward: Ships, Sea and Harbour, one ship, the line's first.
  • Escapement: Clockwork, Brass and the Machine Room, steam and brass indoors.
